title.narrative: Hurricane Rafael: support sexual and reproductive health services and needs of vulnerable persons in affected municipalities in Artemisa and Mayabeque municipality.

description.narrative: This proposal is aimed at two critical areas:Revitalize the immediate capacity of SRH services in the nine municipalities most affected by Hurricane Rafael, including hospitals where maternal health care services are provided, family planning and STI/HIV services in community clinics and local primary health care services, and sexual violence care at the municipal level. It is expected to prevent neonatal and maternal morbidity and mortality, ensure access to contraception, provide STI treatment to young people, ensure care for victims of sexual violence. With the proposal, it will be possible to save the lives of pregnant women, people with STI/HIV, prevent unintended pregnancies, and mitigate the consequences of sexual violence.UNFPA will work with the Ministry of Health (MoH), in particular with the National Mother and Child Program and the Center for Health Promotion and Disease Prevention, and with the Federation of Cuban Women (FMC- CSO).Protect specific vulnerable groups by providing dignity kits (DK) according to local needs. The project will procure and distribute culturally appropriate DK to ensure hygienic and quality living conditions for pregnant women, women of reproductive age (WRA), adolescents, LGBTI, persons with disabilities and their families, and families who have completely lost their homes.UNFPA will work with the FMC, taking into account that there are participating in the community-level damage assessment and community brigades will be organized with the participation of the FMC and MoH to support the implementation of life-saving actions.Since gender inequalities are reinforced in humanitarian settings, the dignity kits will contribute to empowering women and girls, avoiding discrimination and exposure to situations that are frequently linked to harassment and expressions of GBV. Based on UNFPA's internal experience in the implementation of the MISP, the main activities are the acquisition of sexual and reproductive kits (contraceptives, condoms, medications for complications of abortion, STI medications, post-rape treatment kits and equipment). Also, will be acquire medicines and vitamins to support maternal health.At the same time, the proposal will ensure the acquisition of towels and sheets. Awareness, communication and information initiatives will be implemented for decision makers, health providers, representatives of community organizations and beneficiaries. The community brigades support all of this actions. Gender mainstreaming and the human rights approach are strategic axes for the objectives.These actions are focused on the nine most affected municipalities: from Artemisa province: Artemisa, San Antonio de los Baños, Alquízar, Guira de Melena, Mariel, Bahía Honda and Guanajay; from Mayabeque province: Batabanó and Quivicán.Support for the maintenance of SRH services will be complemented by USD 82,000 already approved from the agency's emergency funds. UNFPA is in constant exchange with PAHO, leader of the health cluster, to ensure the complementarity of the actions carried out and the objectives of the proposal. In this case, UNFPA will be supporting, jointly with the MoH, the area of SRH, both the sustainability of life-saving services and the availability of supplies, including DK, focusing on pregnant women, adolescents, trans people, and other groups in conditions of vulnerability. It also includes communication & information actions also aimed at preventing maternal mortality and morbidity, STI, and GBV. Related to procurement, UNFPA will acquire the IARH kits, complementing the scope of procurement with EF. Equipment will also be purchased for primary and secondary level maternal health services (doppler fetal and sphygmomanometer).Thanks to the intervention undertaken during the response to hurricane Ian during 2022 & 2023 at some health centers and territories, today we can count on personnel trained in the use of IARH and MISP as added value, including representatives of CSO.
